title: How Much Fiber in an Avocado? 10.1g per Avocado
description: Avocado: about 10.1 g of fiber per 1 medium avocado (36% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in an avocado?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Avocados, raw, all commercial varieties

intro: Avocado ranks #1 of 15 fruits on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in avocado by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in an avocado?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists avocados, raw, all commercial varieties at 6.7 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 medium avocado (flesh); 150 g) therefore has about 10.1 g of fiber and 240 calories. That is 36% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 40% of a 25 g day and 26% of a 38 g day.

A whole avocado carries more fiber than almost any other fruit, but it is also calorie-dense, so most people eat a third to a half at a time. Avocado fat and fiber together are part of why it is filling.

sections.heading: Portion sizes and guacamole
paragraphs: U.S. Nutrition Facts labels use one-third of a medium avocado (50 g) as the serving. In practice, half an avocado on toast or in a bowl is more common.
Guacamole is mostly avocado plus onion, tomato, lime, and salt. A 2-tablespoon scoop is small; the calculator has a guacamole entry if you log it that way.

sections.heading: How avocado compares with other fruits
paragraphs: Of the 15 fruits on this site, avocado ranks #1 for fiber per typical serving and #10 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 4.2 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [raspberries](/fiber-in-raspberries) at 8 g (1 cup); [blackberries](/fiber-in-blackberries) at 7.6 g (1 cup); [pear](/fiber-in-pear) at 5.5 g (1 medium). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), avocado is #30 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding avocado to your day
paragraphs: Half an avocado on two slices of whole-grain toast is a breakfast in the 10 g range. Avocado also pairs naturally with beans in a burrito bowl.

Example: 1/2 avocado, 2 slices whole wheat bread, 1 egg. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 8.8 g of fiber, with 5 g from the avocado. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of avocado?
faqs.a: 6.7 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Avocados, raw, all commercial varieties). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in avocado (1/2 medium avocado)?
faqs.a: About 5 g, for 75 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in half an avocado?
faqs.a: About 5 g for half of a medium avocado (about 75 g of flesh), using USDA’s average for all commercial varieties. Large Florida avocados are much bigger, so weigh them if you can.
Yes, botanically it is a single-seeded berry. Nutritionally it behaves more like a fat source with unusually high fiber.
